paragraphs: In this report, unless the context suggests otherwise, references to the "Company" or "FirstSun" refers to FirstSun Capital Bancorp, a Delaware corporation, and references to "we," "us," and "our" refer to the combined business of FirstSun Capital Bancorp and its wholly-owned subsidiaries, including Sunflower Bank, National Association ("Sunflower Bank" or the "Bank"), Sunflower Wealth Advisors LLC, and FEIF Capital Partners, LLC.

We are a financial holding company headquartered in Denver, Colorado, providing a full spectrum of deposit, lending, treasury management, wealth management and online banking products and services through our two primary operating subsidiaries—Sunflower Bank, a national banking association headquartered in Dallas, Texas, that operates as Sunflower Bank, N.A. and First National 1870, a division of Sunflower Bank, N.A., and Sunflower Wealth Advisors LLC, a registered investment advisor organized under the laws of the State of Kansas that provides discretionary investment management to retail and institutional accounts. FirstSun has a third wholly-owned subsidiary, FEIF Capital Partners, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, which is planned to serve as the investment manager of a prospective credit fund.

Sunflower Bank was founded in 1892 and offers a full range of specialized financial services to business customers as well as relationship-focused services to meet personal, business and wealth management financial objectives for its customers throughout Texas, Kansas, Colorado, New Mexico, Arizona, California and Washington and a mortgage lending platform with capabilities in 44 states. Our product line includes commercial and industrial loans and commercial real estate loans, residential mortgage and other consumer loans, a variety of commercial, consumer and private banking deposit products, including noninterest-bearing accounts, interest-bearing demand products, savings accounts, money market accounts and certificates of deposit. Additionally, Sunflower Bank provides treasury management products and services and together with Sunflower Wealth Advisors offers wealth management and trust products including private banking, personal trust and agency accounts, employee benefit and retirement related trust and agency accounts, investment management and advisory agency accounts, and foundation and endowment trust and agency accounts.

As of December 31, 2025, we had consolidated total assets of $8.5 billion, total net loans held-for-investment of $6.6 billion, total deposits of $7.1 billion and total stockholders' equity of $1.2 billion.

On October 27, 2025, we entered into a merger agreement with First Foundation, the holding company of First Foundation Bank, headquartered in Irvine, California, as amended by amendment no. 1 to the merger agreement dated February 6, 2026. Under the merger agreement, First Foundation will merge with and into FirstSun, with FirstSun continuing as the surviving entity. Immediately following the merger, First Foundation Bank will merge with and into Sunflower Bank, with Sunflower Bank continuing as the surviving bank. The consummation of the proposed merger will expand our markets in California and Texas, as well as add new markets in Florida, Nevada and Hawaii.

The merger agreement, as amended, was unanimously approved by the boards of directors of FirstSun and First Foundation, and is subject to customary closing conditions, including receipt of remaining required regulatory approvals. The stockholders of FirstSun and First Foundation approved the merger agreement and transactions contemplated thereby at special stockholders' meetings held on February 27, 2026. The merger is expected to close early in the second quarter of 2026.

We were originally incorporated in the State of Kansas on November 9, 1981, as Handi-Bancshares, Inc., to serve as the holding company of Sunflower Bank (formerly The First National Bank and Trust Company of Salina), before we changed our name to Sunflower Financial, Inc. in 2008. We subsequently changed our name to FirstSun Capital Bancorp and simultaneously reincorporated under the laws of the State of Delaware in June 2017. The subsequent name change and reincorporation were completed pursuant to the merger agreement entered into on July 28, 2016, by and among FirstSun, Strategic Growth Bank Incorporated, which we refer to as "SGB," Strategic Growth Bancorp Incorporated, which we refer to as "Strategic" and First National Bancorp Incorporated, which we refer to as "FNB," and together with SGB and Strategic, as the "SGB parties."

On June 19, 2017, we completed our merger with the SGB parties. Under the merger agreement for the SGB mergers, FirstSun also acquired Guardian Mortgage Company, Inc., which we refer to as "Guardian," a former subsidiary of Strategic. Guardian was merged with and into Sunflower Bank. With the SGB mergers, we acquired two branches in El Paso, Texas and 21 branches in New Mexico and Colorado, as well as residential mortgage loan origination and servicing activities in 13 states. We also relocated our headquarters from Salina, Kansas to Denver, Colorado.

On April 1, 2022, FirstSun completed its merger with Pioneer Bancshares, Inc. ("Pioneer"). Pioneer's wholly-owned subsidiary, Pioneer Bank, SSB, a Texas state savings bank, was merged with and into the Bank, with the Bank continuing as the surviving bank. With the merger, we acquired 19 branches in Texas.
In November 2023, the Bank relocated its main office from Denver, Colorado, to Dallas, Texas.
In December 2024, we made the decision to rebrand our mortgage division as Sunflower Bank Mortgage Lending and cease operating under the Guardian Mortgage tradename.
In June 2025, we made the decision to rebrand our registered investment advisor as Sunflower Wealth Advisors LLC and cease operating under the Logia Portfolio Management tradename.

In November 2025, we established Sunflower Insurance Solutions Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Sunflower Bank, N.A. Sunflower Insurance Solutions will offer life, long-term care and disability coverage, alongside estate planning and generational wealth transfer solutions.

We currently operate our principal executive office at 1400 16th Street, Suite 250, Denver, Colorado 80202, with Sunflower Bank's main office at 8117 Preston Road, Suite 220, Dallas, Texas 75225. We have a model of delivering relationship-driven banking services with local decision-making to communities throughout Texas, Kansas, Colorado, New Mexico, Arizona, California and Washington. The Bank's national lines of business include specialty commercial services and a mortgage lending platform with capabilities in 44 states.

headings: Risks Related to Our Pending Merger with First Foundation

Combining FirstSun and First Foundation may be more difficult, costly or time-consuming than expected, and the anticipated benefits and cost savings of the merger and the bank merger may not be realized.

All regulatory approvals may not be received, may take longer than expected, or may impose conditions that are not presently anticipated or that could have an adverse effect on the combined company following the merger.
The success of the merger and the bank merger and integration of FirstSun and First Foundation will depend on a number of uncertain factors.
Stockholder litigation could prevent or delay the completion of the merger or otherwise negatively impact our business and operations.
Issuance of shares of our common stock in connection with the merger may adversely affect the market price of our common stock.
Risks Related to Our Business, Industry, Markets and Market Interest Rates
Inflationary pressures present a potential threat to our results of operation and financial condition.
Our trust and wealth management business may be negatively impacted by changes in economic and market conditions and clients may seek legal remedies for investment performance.
We are subject to interest rate risk, which could adversely affect our financial condition and profitability.
Our cost of funds may increase as a result of general economic conditions, FDIC insurance assessments, interest rates and competitive pressures.
We are exposed to the possibility that more prepayments may be made by customers to pay down loan balances, which could reduce our interest income and profitability.
We could experience a loss due to competition with other financial institutions.
Consumers may decide not to use banks to complete their financial transactions.
Failure to keep pace with technological change could adversely affect our business.
We may be adversely affected by the lack of soundness of other financial institutions.
The value of securities in our investment portfolio may decline in the future.
Our deposit insurance premiums could be higher in the future, which could have an adverse effect on our future earnings.
Risks Related to Our Lending and Mortgage Banking Activities
If we fail to effectively manage credit risk, our business and financial condition will suffer.
Our allowance for credit losses in our loan portfolio may prove to be inadequate, which may adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
We are exposed to higher credit risk by commercial and industrial and commercial real estate lending.
A significant portion of our loan portfolio is secured by real estate, and events that negatively impact the real estate market could hurt our business.
Nonperforming assets take significant time and resources to resolve and adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.
Our mortgage revenue is cyclical and sensitive to changes in interest rates, economic conditions, housing prices and other factors which would adversely impact our profitability.
We are subject to certain risks related to originating and selling mortgage loans that could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.
We may be required to repurchase mortgage loans or indemnify buyers against losses in some circumstances, which could harm our liquidity, results of operations and financial condition.
paragraphs: An investment in our securities involves various risks, many of which are beyond our control, which could cause our results to differ significantly from management's expectations. Some of these risk factors are described below. Any risk factor discussed below could, by itself or together with one or more other factors, materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations and/or financial condition, and cause the loss of part or all of the value of an investment in FirstSun. Additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or that we currently consider to not be material also may materially and adversely affect us and the value of an investment in our securities. In assessing these risks, you should also refer to other information disclosed in this Form 10-K (and in our subsequent SEC filings), including the financial statements and notes thereto. Any of the risks discussed below could also cause our actual results to differ materially from those discussed, anticipated or implied in these forward-looking statements. See "CAUTIONARY NOTE REGARDING FORWARD-LOOKING STATEMENTS" above in this report.

FirstSun and First Foundation have operated and, until the completion of the merger, must continue to operate, independently. The success of the merger and the bank merger, including anticipated benefits and cost savings, will depend, in part, on our ability to successfully combine and integrate our businesses with First Foundation in a manner that permits growth opportunities and does not materially disrupt the existing customer relations or result in decreased revenues due to loss of customers. In addition, the success of the merger will depend, in part, on the successful execution of the planned balance sheet repositioning strategy which contemplates the sale or disposition of certain assets of First Foundation and pay down or run off certain liabilities of First Foundation as part of the balance sheet repositioning (the "balance sheet repositioning"). Execution of the balance sheet repositioning will inherently be subject to market conditions. There is a risk that such conditions will be less favorable than anticipated when the parties entered into the merger agreement and that the balance sheet repositioning may not have the expected effects on our net interest margin, liquidity, or portfolio positioning for potential changes in interest rates. If we are unable to successfully achieve these objectives, the anticipated benefits of the merger and the bank merger may not be realized fully or at all or may take longer to realize than expected. In addition, the actual cost savings of the merger and the bank merger could be less than anticipated, and integration may result in additional and unforeseen expenses.

An inability to realize the full extent of the anticipated benefits of the merger, as well as any delays encountered in the integration process and the implementation of the balance sheet repositioning, could have an adverse effect upon the revenues, levels of expenses and operating results of the combined company, which may adversely affect the value of our common stock after the completion of the merger. It is possible that the integration process could result in the loss of key employees, the disruption of either company's ongoing businesses or inconsistencies in standards, controls, procedures and policies that adversely affect the combined company's ability to maintain relationships with clients, customers, depositors and employees or to achieve the anticipated benefits and cost savings of the merger and the bank merger. If we experience difficulties with the integration process, the anticipated benefits of the merger and the bank merger may not be realized fully or at all, or may take longer to realize than expected. As with any merger of financial institutions, there also may be business disruptions that cause us and/or First Foundation to lose customers or cause customers to remove their accounts from us and/or First Foundation and move their business to competing financial institutions. Integration efforts between the two companies will also divert management attention and resources. These integration matters could have an adverse effect on each of us and First Foundation during this transition period and for an undetermined period after completion of the merger on the combined company.

Furthermore, the board of directors and executive leadership of the combined companies following the merger will consist of former directors and executive officers from each of FirstSun and First Foundation, as described in the merger agreement. Combining the boards of directors and management teams of each company into a single board and a single management team could require the reconciliation of differing priorities and philosophies.

Before the merger and the bank merger may be completed, various approvals, consents and non-objections must be obtained. While we have received approval for the bank merger from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, the merger and the bank merger remains subject to approval from the Federal Reserve Board and various other antitrust, insurance and other authorities in the United States. Other approvals, waivers or consents from regulators may also be

required. In determining whether to grant these approvals, the regulators consider a variety of factors, including the regulatory standing of each party. These approvals could be delayed or not obtained at all, including due to: an adverse development in either party's regulatory standing or in any other factors considered by regulators when granting such approvals; governmental, political or community group inquiries, investigations or opposition; or changes in legislation or the political environment generally. These regulators also could impose conditions on the completion of the merger or the bank merger or require changes to the terms of the merger or the bank merger. Such conditions or changes could have the effect of delaying or preventing completion of the merger or the bank merger or imposing additional costs on or limiting the revenues of the combined company following the merger and the bank merger, any of which might have an adverse effect on the combined company following the merger.

paragraphs: MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS OF FIRSTSUN

In this section, unless the context suggests otherwise, references to "we," "us," and "our" mean the combined business of FirstSun and its wholly-owned subsidiaries, Sunflower Bank, Sunflower Wealth Advisors, LLC, and FEIF Capital Partners, LLC.

The following discussion is an analysis of our consolidated results of operations for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, and financial condition for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024. This discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and accompanying footnotes filed with this report in "Part II, Item 8. Financial Statements." We have omitted discussion of 2023 results where it would be redundant to the discussion previously included in "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations of FirstSun" section of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024, filed with the SEC on March 7, 2025. Historical results of operations and the percentage relationships among any amounts included, and any trends that may appear, may not indicate trends in operations or results of operations for any future periods.

Comments regarding our business that are not historical facts are considered forward-looking statements that involve inherent risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those contained in these forward-looking statements. For additional information regarding our cautionary disclosures, see the "Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" beginning on page 3 of this report.

FirstSun Capital Bancorp, headquartered in Denver, Colorado, is the financial holding company for Sunflower Bank, National Association, which is headquartered in Dallas, Texas and operates as Sunflower Bank, First National 1870 and Sunflower Bank Mortgage Lending. We conduct a full-service community banking and trust business through our wholly-owned subsidiaries—Sunflower Bank, Sunflower Wealth Advisors, LLC and FEIF Capital Partners, LLC.

We offer a full range of relationship-focused services to meet our clients' personal, business and wealth management financial objectives throughout Texas, Kansas, Colorado, New Mexico, Arizona, California and Washington and a mortgage lending platform with capabilities in 44 states. Our product line includes commercial and industrial loans, commercial real estate loans, residential mortgage, public finance and other consumer loans, and a variety of commercial and consumer deposit products, including noninterest-bearing accounts, interest-bearing demand products, savings accounts, money market accounts and certificates of deposit. We also offer wealth management and trust products including personal trust and agency accounts, employee benefit and retirement related trust and agency accounts, investment management and advisory agency accounts, and foundation and endowment trust and agency accounts. We also offer online banking and bill payment services, online cash management, safe deposit box rentals, debit card and ATM card services and the availability of a network of ATMs for our customers.

We operate FirstSun through two operating segments: Banking and Mortgage Operations. We also allocate certain expenses to Corporate, which is not an operating segment. The expenses included in Corporate are not deemed to be allocable to our operating segments. The operating segments have been determined based on the products and services we offer and reflect the manner in which our financial information is evaluated by management. Each of the operating segments is complementary to each other and because of the interrelationship of the segments, the information presented is not indicative of how the segments would perform if they operated as independent entities. For additional information on our segments, see Note 21 - Segment Information included in our consolidated financial statements included elsewhere in this report.

On October 27, 2025, we entered into a merger agreement with First Foundation, the holding company of First Foundation Bank, headquartered in Irvine, California, as amended by amendment no. 1 to the merger agreement dated February 6, 2026. Under the merger agreement, First Foundation will merge with and into FirstSun, with FirstSun continuing as the surviving entity. Immediately following the merger, First Foundation Bank will merge with and into Sunflower Bank, with Sunflower Bank continuing as the surviving bank. The consummation of the proposed merger will expand our markets in California and Texas, as well as add new markets in Florida, Nevada and Hawaii.

The merger agreement, as amended, was unanimously approved by the boards of directors of FirstSun and First Foundation, and is subject to customary closing conditions, including receipt of remaining required regulatory approvals. The stockholders of FirstSun and First Foundation approved the merger agreement and transactions contemplated thereby at special stockholders' meetings held on February 27, 2026. The merger is expected to close early in the second quarter of 2026.
We delivered strong financial results in 2025, compared to 2024, which included:
•Net income of $97.9 million, $3.47 per diluted share (adjusted net income of $100.5 million1, $3.56 adjusted per diluted share1)
•Return on average total assets of 1.18% (adjusted return on average total assets of 1.21%1)
•Return on average stockholders' equity of 8.88% (adjusted return on average stockholders' equity of 9.11%1)
•Loan growth of 4.7% •Average deposit growth of 6.6%

paragraphs: 本報告中，除非上下文另有說明，否則提及「本公司」或「FirstSun」均指 FirstSun Capital Bancorp，一家設立於德國的公司，提及「我們」、「我們」及「我們」均指 FirstSun Capital Bancorp 及其全資子公司，包括 Sunflower Bank, National Association（「Sunflower Bank」或「銀行」）、Sunflower Wealth Advisors LLC 與 FEIF Capital Partners, LLC 的合併業務。

我們是一家財務控股公司，總部設於科羅拉多州丹佛市，透過我們兩大主要營運子公司，提供完整的存款、貸款、財務管理、財富管理與網際網路銀行產品與服務—Sunflower Bank，一家總部設於德克薩斯州達拉斯市的國家銀行協會，經營為 Sunflower Bank, N.A.，以及 First National 1870，為 Sunflower Bank, N.A. 的一個部門，以及 Sunflower Wealth Advisors LLC，一家根據堪薩斯州法律設立的註冊投資顧問公司，為零售與機構帳戶提供投資管理服務。FirstSun 還有一家第三家全資子公司 FEIF Capital Partners, LLC，一家設立於德國的有限責任公司，預計將擔任一個潛在信貸基金的投資管理人。

Sunflower Bank 於 1892 年成立，為其商業客戶提供廣泛的專業金融服務，並為其客戶在德克薩斯州、堪薩斯州、科羅拉多州、新墨西哥州、亞利桑那州、加利福尼亞州與華盛頓州提供以關係為導向的服務，以達成個人、商業與財富管理的財務目標，並提供一個房貸貸款平台，可在 44 個州運作。我們的產品線包括商業與工業貸款與商業不動產貸款、住宅房貸與其他消費者貸款、以及多種商業、消費者與私人銀行存款產品，包括無息帳戶、有息活期產品、儲蓄帳戶、貨幣市場帳戶與定期存款。此外，Sunflower Bank 還提供財務管理產品與服務，並與 Sunflower Wealth Advisors 合作提供財富管理與信託產品，包括私人銀行、個人信託與代理帳戶、員工福利與退休相關信託與代理帳戶、投資管理與顧問代理帳戶，以及基金會與終身基金信託與代理帳戶。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的合併總資產為 8.5 十億美元，總貸款持有為投資為 6.6 十億美元，總存款為 7.1 十億美元，總股東權益為 1.2 十億美元。

2025 年 10 月 27 日，我們與 First Foundation 籤訂了合併協議，First Foundation 為 First Foundation Bank 的控股公司，總部設於加州爾灣市，此協議經 2026 年 2 月 6 日的協議修正案修正。根據合併協議，First Foundation 將與 FirstSun 合併，FirstSun 繼續為存續公司。合併後，First Foundation Bank 將與 Sunflower Bank 合併，Sunflower Bank 繼續為存續銀行。此預期合併的完成將擴大我們在加州與德州的市場，並新增佛羅裏達州、內華達州與夏威夷州的新市場。
修正後的合併協議已獲得 FirstSun 與 First Foundation 董事會一致批准，並需符合慣常的關閉條件，包括取得剩餘必要的監管批准。FirstSun 與 First Foundation 的股東已在 2026 年 2 月 27 日舉行的特別股東會議上批准此合併協議與相關交易。預計此合併將於 2026 年第二季初期完成。

我們最初於 1981 年 11 月 9 日在堪薩斯州註冊成立，名為 Handi-Bancshares, Inc.，以作為 Sunflower Bank（原為 The First National Bank and Trust Company of Salina）的控股公司，我們於 2008 年將公司名稱改為 Sunflower Financial, Inc.。我們隨後於 2017 年 6 月將公司名稱改為 FirstSun Capital Bancorp，並同時根據德國法律重新註冊。此後的公司名稱變更與重新註冊係根據 2016 年 7 月 28 日簽訂的合併協議完成，該協議由 FirstSun、Strategic Growth Bank Incorporated（我們稱為「SGB」）、Strategic Growth Bancorp Incorporated（我們稱為「Strategic」）與 First National Bancorp Incorporated（我們稱為「FNB」）簽訂，與 SGB 與 Strategic 一同稱為「SGB parties」。

2017 年 6 月 19 日，我們完成了與 SGB parties 的合併。根據 SGB 合併協議，FirstSun 也取得了 Guardian Mortgage Company, Inc.（我們稱為「Guardian」），為 Strategic 的前子公司。Guardian 與 Sunflower Bank 合併。透過 SGB 合併，我們取得了位於德州 El Paso 的兩家分行，以及位於新墨西哥州與科羅拉多州的 21 家分行，以及在 13 個州的住宅房貸貸款發放與服務業務。我們也將總部從堪薩斯州的 Salina 移至科羅拉多州的丹佛市。
2022年4月1日，FirstSun完成與Pioneer Bancshares, Inc.（"Pioneer"）的合併。Pioneer的 wholly-owned subsidiary，Pioneer Bank, SSB，為德克薩斯州的儲蓄銀行，與Bank合併，Bank繼續作為存續銀行。透過此次合併，我們取得德克薩斯州19家分行。
2023年11月，Bank將總部從科羅拉多州丹佛遷至德克薩斯州達拉斯。
2024年12月，我們決定將房貸部門重新品牌為Sunflower Bank Mortgage Lending，並停止以Guardian Mortgage為品牌營運。
2025年6月，我們決定將註冊投資顧問重新品牌為Sunflower Wealth Advisors LLC，並停止以Logia Portfolio Management為品牌營運。
2025年11月，我們成立Sunflower Insurance Solutions Inc.，為Sunflower Bank, N.A.的 wholly owned subsidiary。Sunflower Insurance Solutions將提供壽險、長期照護及殘障保障，以及遺產規劃與世代財富傳承解決方案。

paragraphs: 管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析
在本節中，除非上下文另有說明，否則提及 "we," "us," 和 "our" 指的是 FirstSun 及其全資子公司 Sunflower Bank、Sunflower Wealth Advisors, LLC 與 FEIF Capital Partners, LLC 的合併業務。

以下討論為我們合併財務報表所載 2025 年 12 月 31 日、2024 年 12 月 31 日及 2023 年 12 月 31 日之營運成果分析，以及 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日之財務狀況。此討論與分析應與我們合併財務報表及相關附註說明，載於本報告 "Part II, Item 8. 財務報表" 部分一併閱讀。我們已省略 2023 年之結果討論，因與 "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations of FirstSun" 節中已包含之內容重複。歷史營運成果及任何金額間的百分比關係，以及任何可能出現的趨勢，可能無法反映未來期間之營運或結果。
關於我們業務之說明，若非歷史事實，則被視為前瞻性陳述，涉及內在風險與不確定性。實際結果可能與這些前瞻性陳述中所載內容有重大差異。有關我們警示性披露之額外資訊，請參閱本報告第 3 頁開始的 "Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements"。
FirstSun Capital Bancorp 設立於科羅拉多州丹佛市，為 Sunflower Bank, National Association（設立於德克薩斯州達拉斯市，營運為 Sunflower Bank, First National 1870 及 Sunflower Bank Mortgage Lending）之金融控股公司。

我們透過全資子公司 Sunflower Bank、Sunflower Wealth Advisors, LLC 與 FEIF Capital Partners, LLC 提供全面的社區銀行與信託業務。我們為客戶在德克薩斯州、堪薩斯州、科羅拉多州、新墨西哥州、亞利桑那州、加利福尼亞州與華盛頓州提供個人、企業與財富管理之財務目標服務，並提供於 44 個州運作之房貸貸款平台。我們的產品線包括商業與工業貸款、商業不動產貸款、住宅房貸、公營財務及其它消費者貸款，以及多種商業與消費者存款產品，包括免息帳戶、有息活期產品、儲蓄帳戶、貨幣市場帳戶及定期存款。我們也提供財富管理與信託產品，包括個人信託與代理帳戶、員工福利與退休相關信託與代理帳戶、投資管理與顧問代理帳戶，以及財團與永續基金信託與代理帳戶。我們也提供網銀與帳單支付服務、線上現金管理、保險箱租賃、提款卡與 ATM 卡服務，以及為客戶提供 ATM 網路的使用。
我們透過兩個營運分部進行 FirstSun 之營運：銀行與房貸營運。我們也將部分費用歸屬於企業部門，該部門並非營運分部。歸屬於企業部門之費用不被視為可歸屬於營運分部。營運分部之劃分係根據我們所提供的產品與服務，並反映管理層評估財務資訊的方式。每個營運分部之間為互補關係，因分部間之相互關聯，所呈現之資訊並不能反映各分部如為獨立運作時之表現。

於 2025 年 10 月 27 日，我們與 First Foundation（First Foundation Bank 之控股公司，設立於加州爾灣市）簽訂合併協議，該協議經 2026 年 2 月 6 日之協議修正案修正。根據合併協議，First Foundation 將與 FirstSun 合併，FirstSun 繼續為存續公司。合併後立即，First Foundation Bank 將與 Sunflower Bank 合併，Sunflower Bank 繼續為存續銀行。預期合併之完成將擴大我們在加州與德克薩斯州之市場，並新增佛羅裏達州、內華達州與夏威夷州之新市場。
合併協議，經修正後，已獲得 FirstSun 與 First Foundation 董事會一致批准，並受慣常關閉條件限制，包括取得剩餘所需監管批准。FirstSun 與 First Foundation 的股東已於 2026 年 2 月 27 日舉行的特別股東大會上批准合併協議及相關交易。預期該合併將於 2026 年第二季初期完成。
我們在 2025 年的財務表現較 2024 年強勁，包括：
•淨收入為 97.9 百萬美元，每股稀釋後收益為 3.47 美元（調整後淨收入為 100.5 百萬美元1，調整後每股稀釋後收益為 3.56 美元1）
•平均總資產回報率為 1.18%（調整後平均總資產回報率為 1.21%1）
•平均股東權益回報率為 8.88%（調整後平均股東權益回報率為 9.11%1）
•貸款成長為 4.7% •平均存款成長為 6.6%

headings: 與 First Foundation 進行待定合併之相關風險
FirstSun 與 First Foundation 結合可能比預期更困難、成本更高或耗時更久，且合併後預期的效益與成本節省可能無法實現。
所有監管機構的批准可能無法取得、耗時長於預期，或施加的條件與目前預期不同，且可能對合併後之公司產生不利影響。
合併與銀行合併及 FirstSun 與 First Foundation 整合的成功，將取決於許多不確定因素。
股東訴訟可能導致合併無法完成或延遲，或對本公司之業務與運作產生負面影響。
為合併發行本公司普通股可能對本公司普通股之市場價格產生不利影響。
與本公司業務、產業、市場及市場利率相關之風險
通貨膨脹壓力可能對本公司之營運成果與財務狀況造成潛在威脅。
本公司信託及資產管理業務可能因經濟與市場條件變動而受到負面影響，客戶可能針對投資績效尋求法律救濟。
本公司面臨利率風險，此風險可能對本公司財務狀況及獲利能力產生不利影響。
本公司之資金成本可能因總體經濟條件、FDIC 保險費率、利率及競爭壓力而增加。
本公司可能因客戶提前償還貸款以減少貸款餘額，而導致利息收入及獲利能力下降。
本公司可能因與其他金融機構之競爭而遭受損失。
消費者可能決定不透過銀行完成其財務交易。
未能跟上科技變革可能對本公司業務產生不利影響。
本公司可能因其他金融機構之財務健全性不足而受到不利影響。
本公司投資組閤中證券的價值可能於未來下降。
本公司存款保險費率可能於未來提高，這可能會對本公司未來獲利產生不利影響。
與本公司貸款及房貸業務活動相關的風險
若本公司無法有效管理信用風險，將會對本公司業務及財務狀況造成損害。
本公司貸款組閤中的信用損失備抵可能不足，這可能會對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
本公司因商業及工業貸款及商業不動產貸款而面臨較高的信用風險。
本公司貸款組閤中有一大部份是以不動產為擔保，而對不動產市場產生負面影響的事件可能會損害本公司業務。
不良資產需要大量時間及資源才能解決，並會對本公司營運成果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
本公司之房貸收入具有週期性，且對利率變動、經濟情勢、房價及其他因素敏感，這些因素可能對本公司獲利造成不利影響。
本公司面臨與發放及銷售房貸貸款相關之風險，這些風險可能對本公司財務狀況及營運成果產生重大不利影響。
在某些情況下，本公司可能需買回房貸貸款或賠償買方之損失，此舉可能影響本公司流動性、營運成果及財務狀況。
paragraphs: 投資本公司證券涉及多種風險，許多風險超出本公司控制範圍，可能導致本公司結果與管理階層預期產生顯著差異。部分風險因素於下文說明。任何於下文討論的風險因素，單獨或與一個或多個其他因素共同作用，均可能對本公司業務、營運結果及/或財務狀況造成重大且不利影響，並導致投資於第一陽光之價值喪失部分或全部。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前本公司尚未知悉或認為不具重大性，也可能對本公司及投資於本公司證券之價值造成重大且不利影響。評估這些風險時，您應同時參考本Form 10-K（及本公司後續向美國證券交易委員會提交之申報文件）所披露之其他資訊，包括財務報表及其附註。任何於下文討論之風險因素，也可能導致本公司實際結果與本報告中所討論、預期或暗示之預測性陳述產生重大差異。請參閱本報告上方之「預測性陳述警示說明」。

第一陽光與第一財團已運作，並在合併完成前必須繼續獨立運作。合併之成功與銀行合併之成功，包括預期之好處與成本節省，部分取決於本公司能否以允許成長機會且不嚴重幹擾現有客戶關係、不因客戶流失而導致收入減少之方式，成功整合與第一財團之業務。此外，合併之成功部分取決於成功執行預計之資產負債表重整策略，該策略預期出售或處分第一財團之部分資產，並償還或減少第一財團之部分負債，作為資產負債表重整之一環（稱為「資產負債表重整」）。執行資產負債表重整將 inherently 受市場條件影響。存在風險，即這些條件可能不如合併協議簽訂時預期之有利，且資產負債表重整可能無法產生預期之效果於本公司淨利息邊際、流動性或潛在利率變動之資產組合定位。若本公司無法成功達成這些目標，則合併與銀行合併預期之好處可能無法完全或完全實現，或實現時間可能比預期延後。此外，合併與銀行合併之實際成本節省可能低於預期，整合過程可能導致額外且未預見之費用。

無法實現合併預期之全部好處，以及整合過程遭遇任何延誤與資產負債表重整之執行，可能對合併後之公司之收入、費用水準與營運結果產生不利影響，可能對合併後之公司之普通股價值產生不利影響。有可能整合過程導致關鍵員工流失、任一公司之持續業務受幹擾，或標準、控制、程序與政策之不一致，不利於合併後之公司維持與客戶、客戶、存款人及員工之關係，或達成合併與銀行合併預期之好處與成本節省。若本公司遭遇整合過程困難，則合併與銀行合併預期之好比可能無法完全或完全實現，或實現時間可能比預期延後。如同任何金融機構合併，也可能產生業務中斷，導致本公司及/或第一財團失去客戶，或導致客戶將帳戶從本公司及/或第一財團移轉至競爭性金融機構。兩家公司之間之整合努力亦將分散管理階層之注意力與資源。這些整合事項可能在過渡期間對本公司與第一財團產生不利影響，並在合併完成後對合併後之公司產生無法預測之影響。
此外，合併後之公司董事會與執行領導層將由第一陽光與第一財團之前董事與執行長組成，如合併協議所述。將兩家公司之董事會與管理團隊整合為單一董事會與單一管理團隊，可能需要協調不同之優先順序與理念。
在合併與銀行合併完成前，必須取得多種批准、同意與無異議。雖然本公司已獲得美國貨幣監理署對銀行合併之批准，但合併與銀行合併仍需獲得聯邦儲備銀行與美國其他反壟斷、保險及其他主管機關之批准。其他來自監管機構之批准、豁免或同意

可能為必要。在決定是否授予這些批准時，監管機構會考量多種因素，包括各當事方之監管地位。這些批准可能被延宕或完全無法取得，包括因：任一方之監管地位出現不利發展，或因監管機構在授予這些批准時考量之任何其他因素；政府、政治或社區團體之查詢、調查或反對；或法律法規或政治環境之變動。這些監管機構亦可能對合併或銀行合併之完成施加條件，或要求修改合併或銀行合併之條款。這些條件或修改可能導致延宕或阻止合併或銀行合併之完成，或對合併後之公司施加額外成本或限制其收入，任何情況均可能對合併後之公司產生不利影響。
